A1.justification: Both complete 19-page PDFs describe Speech-Hands. The text, mathematical notation, five figures, nine tables, and Appendices A-F support reliable comparison despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original ASR and AudioQA experiments, action-token analyses, and the DSP tool-calling experiment in Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains the original ASR and AudioQA results, action-token analyses, and Appendix C tool-calling experiment.

M1.justification: The action tokens, labeling rules, majority-sampling strategy, training objective, and inference procedure are unchanged. The ASR prompt moves from Appendix B to Section 3.4; Appendix C's DSP tool extension already exists in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same seven ASR benchmarks and three MD-Audio/DCASE2025 AudioQA subsets. Appendix C also retains the same AMI, VoxPopuli, Soundscape QA, and Complex QA evaluations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches between v1 Tables 1-2 and v2 Tables 3-4, including the ASR/omni models, cascaded GER, AudioFlamingo 3, and SFT/GRPO comparisons. The preliminary and Appendix C comparisons are also retained.

E3.justification: Dataset splits and sample counts, WER/accuracy/action-token metrics, and experimental settings are retained. Both specify five training epochs, fp16, batch size 64, learning rate 1e-4 with cosine decay, and greedy decoding.

E4.justification: The prompt ablation and zero-shot confusion analysis move from v1 Appendix A, Tables 5-6, to v2 main-text Tables 1-2. Their evidence is unchanged, as are the action-token analyses, DSP tool study, and case studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-training uncertainty summaries, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The existing five-sample external-prediction strategy is unchanged.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged. Examples include 5.69% average WER for Speech-Hands with Parakeet, 77.37% AudioQA accuracy with majority sampling, and Appendix C's 13.41% AMI WER and 63.15% Soundscape accuracy with tools. Figure 4's confusion-matrix images are identical.

T1.justification: The task formulation, action-set definitions, and WER/correctness-based labeling rules in Section 3 and Appendix C are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contribution: explicit self-reflection through internal/external/rewrite decisions for ASR and AudioQA. The performance, robustness, and interpretability claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations of external misguidance, overcorrection, and sparse rewrite decisions are retained. Limitations concerning token imbalance, restricted ASR training, and untested transfer or multiple-external-model setups are unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a first-page access pointer for the project page, interactive demo, openclaw branch, and code. New acknowledgments mention H100 DGX and LPU support. Existing implementation details remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish the linked resources' completeness.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are retained. Adding Song et al.'s publication year and changing bibliographic fields for Sayigh et al. are metadata edits, without adding research or revising the relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: V2 makes limited organizational and editorial edits: relocating the ASR prompt into Section 3.4, updating cross-references, revising the author/correspondence block, and adding acknowledgments. The scientific narrative remains largely verbatim.

P2.justification: The framework schematic and preliminary bar chart swap Figure 2/3 order. Two appendix tables move into the main text, and the prompt-ablation caption now explains columns (a) and (b). Tables and case boxes reflow, and printed page-number footers disappear; the underlying exhibits are retained.

improvement.justification: The new resource-access footnote and placement of existing preliminary evidence and the ASR prompt alongside their discussion modestly improve usability. The fuller ablation caption also improves readability. Scientific support remains unchanged, while removing printed page numbers creates a small navigation drawback.
